title: Manufacturing transplantable human organs on demand

concept.text: The innovation would be a reproducible way to manufacture durable, human-scale organs that can be transplanted into recipients and provide the integrated functions needed to sustain life. An organ would need the appropriate cell types, internal architecture, blood supply, drainage pathways where required, and coordinated physiological activity. Producing a small tissue model or demonstrating one organ function would be an important intermediate achievement, but would not by itself establish this capability.

Scope synthesis: “On demand” means that production could be planned around clinical need with a predictable manufacturing schedule, quality and supply; it does not imply instantaneous production. The concept encompasses manufacturing a transplantable biological organ, with successful implantation and sustained recipient function as essential tests of the product. It extends beyond the kidney evidence supplied here to other organ types, whose particular functional and structural requirements would need separate demonstrations.

significance.text: Conditional impact synthesis: Reproducibly manufacturing functional organs could change transplantation from a procedure constrained by donor availability into one increasingly planned around patient need. A dependable manufacturing route could make organ supply and treatment scheduling more predictable. The supplied kidney study establishes a technical connection between engineered organoids and the future goal of kidney replacement, rather than demonstrating this change in clinical supply.

Conditional downstream synthesis: A clinically successful manufacturing platform could support more planned transplantation and reduce some delays associated with obtaining a suitable donor organ. Broad access would still depend on affordable production, immune compatibility or effective immune management, surgical capacity and continuing care. Manufacturing alone would not establish universal access, eliminate rejection or make every recipient suitable for transplantation. The analogy to ordinary industrial production is therefore limited: biological function, recipient compatibility and long-term safety would remain requirements for every clinical product.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is the transition from engineered tissue components to a complete replacement organ whose functions remain coordinated at human scale. For a kidney, filtration must be integrated with the rest of renal physiology and a route for urine to leave the tissue. The supplied study explicitly identifies the absence of collecting ducts and consequent lack of urine drainage in its organoids. Vascularized tissue that filters a tracer therefore does not yet constitute a replacement kidney.

Scale and vascular integration are linked engineering barriers. Producing more organoid tissue is not equivalent to organizing that tissue into a human-scale organ with an effective blood supply and coordinated function. The reported integration of human endothelial cells into vascularized kidney organoids advances one part of this problem, while leaving whole-organ architecture, drainage and durable replacement function unresolved in the supplied evidence.

Engineering synthesis: A clinically usable process would also need to produce consistent organs across manufacturing runs, verify their function before release, and maintain performance after implantation. The unresolved task includes connecting the manufactured organ to the recipient, managing its immune interaction and demonstrating durable safety and function. Requirements would differ by organ; success with kidney tissue would not establish that a liver or another vital organ can be manufactured by the same process.

current_state.text: In an article published on 2 February 2026, Murat Tekguc and colleagues reported increased-scale production of vascularized human kidney organoids and size-selective dextran filtration in implanted nephron sheets. The work included human endothelial integration and implantation in immunodeficient mice, with assessments 6–11 days after implantation. It was a nonclinical laboratory study and involved no patients.

The article text described differences in the distribution of 3 kDa and 500 kDa dextrans, together with complementary fixed-tissue localization and an in vitro diffusion control. These observations support the reported component-level finding of size-selective filtration. They do not establish physiological filtration thresholds, adequate whole-body waste clearance, durable renal replacement or human-scale kidney function. The short mouse observation window also does not establish long-term graft performance.

The organoids lacked collecting ducts and could not drain urine. This is a concrete functional gap between the reported filtration experiment and a transplantable replacement kidney. The paper's discussion of implantable bioengineered kidneys manufactured to clinical production requirements describes a future goal. The supplied evidence contains no demonstration of a manufactured liver or of the proposed capability across multiple organ types.

The supplied review had access to full main-article text in both HTML and PDF copies; these are two formats of the same study, not independent replication. Figures, movies and underlying datasets were not independently inspected. Supplementary extraction was partial because some image pages lacked extractable text, although the main article was sufficient to assess the limited reported result. The supplied freshness record is empty, so the evidence does not establish whether this remained the latest result on 1 November 2026 or provide a comprehensive account of the field through that date. These limitations do not invalidate the dated finding.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Reproducibly manufacture durable, human-scale organs and show integrated, life-supporting function in recipients. A convincing demonstration should establish the organ's coordinated physiological contribution, including necessary blood supply and drainage, rather than rely on tissue survival or a single functional assay. Functional endpoints should distinguish the manufactured organ's contribution from residual native-organ function and other life-supporting treatments.
completion_criteria.label: Human-scale organs reproducibly provide durable, integrated life-supporting function

completion_criteria.text: Proposed breadth and reproducibility test: Demonstrate the capability in at least two vital organ types, such as kidney and liver, with independent replication of manufacturing and recipient-function results for each. The two-organ requirement is a proposed test of generality, not a published consensus standard. Success would establish the demonstrated breadth of the platform; it would not prove that every human organ can be manufactured.
completion_criteria.label: Two vital organ types demonstrate independently replicated manufacturing and function

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical and practical boundaries: For each organ type, prespecify clinically meaningful follow-up duration, safety and functional endpoints, and comparisons with conventional transplantation. Assess whether long-term outcomes are comparable under those defined conditions. Demonstrate consistent production across runs and evaluate throughput and total manufacturing and care costs against explicit clinical-use targets. The supplied material does not establish numerical targets for duration, acceptable outcome differences, throughput or cost; those remain to be defined before these criteria could serve as an assessable completion test.
completion_criteria.label: Clinical outcomes and production feasibility assessed against predefined clinical-use targets

related_concepts.text: Conceptual comparison: BME-06, “Long-term banking of transplantable human organs,” concerns preserving organs for later use; BME-01 concerns making them. Manufacturing and banking could jointly improve supply planning, but neither capability establishes the other. BME-12, “Reliable, scalable animal-to-human organ transplantation,” offers another route to organ supply through animal organs, whereas BME-01 targets manufactured human organs. BME-13, “Durable autonomous artificial-organ replacement,” shares the life-supporting replacement objective but centers on artificial-organ systems rather than manufactured biological human organs.

Conceptual comparison: BME-11, “Controlled regeneration of complex organs in the adult body,” seeks to rebuild organs within the patient. BME-17, “Minimally invasive assembly of functional tissue inside the body,” emphasizes assembling tissue in place. Both overlap with BME-01 in tissue organization and functional integration, but their site and mode of construction differ from manufacturing an organ for transplantation.

Conceptual comparison: BME-08, “Reliable, antigen-specific immune tolerance,” could help a manufactured organ remain compatible with its recipient, but immune tolerance does not supply the organ's architecture or physiological function. BME-16, “Long-lived tissue-integrated interfaces for implants,” overlaps with durable integration at the recipient boundary, while BME-01 additionally requires a complete biological organ. Neither supporting capability can be assumed to follow automatically from successful organ manufacture.

Conceptual comparison: BME-10, “Validated patient-specific models for testing treatments before use,” can overlap in its use of engineered human tissues or organoids. Its success criterion is predictive validity for treatment decisions; BME-01 requires life-supporting function after transplantation. A useful kidney model can therefore succeed without qualifying as a replacement kidney. BME-02, “Programmable delivery of genetic therapies to most tissues,” could provide tools for modifying cells or tissues, but delivery alone does not establish whole-organ construction.

Conceptual comparison: BME-05, “Programmable living medicines that sense and respond inside the body,” shares the use of living biological systems as therapy, but targets programmed therapeutic behavior rather than necessarily reconstructing an entire organ. BME-14, “Shelf-stable, broadly compatible replacement for critical blood functions,” also aims to replace biological function, with a distinct target of blood functions, storage stability and compatibility. Neither entry should be treated as equivalent to manufacturing a transplantable solid organ.

Conceptual comparison: BME-03, “Reconstruction of a chronically severed spinal cord,” shares challenges of organized biological repair and functional integration but targets restoration of an existing neural pathway. BME-04, “A durable bidirectional neural interface for movement and sensation,” concerns communication with the nervous system. BME-09, “Physiological extra-uterine support through extreme prematurity,” concerns supporting ongoing development outside the uterus. These are distinct functional objectives rather than demonstrations of organ manufacture.

Conceptual comparison: BME-07, “A broadly effective early-warning test for lethal cancers,” BME-15, “Accessible deep-body molecular imaging,” and BME-18, “Long-lived continuous sensing of multiple clinically useful biomarkers,” concern detection or measurement. Such capabilities could potentially help evaluate manufactured organs or monitor recipients, but their own success criteria concern diagnostic or sensing performance and do not establish transplantable-organ production.

change_log.change: Preserved BME-01's identity and integrated whole-organ function, vascular supply, drainage and durability into the concept explanation.
change_log.reason: The central capability exceeds organoid production, tissue survival or demonstration of one physiological function.

change_log.change: Expanded the February 2026 result with the mouse setting, 6–11-day assessment window, 3 kDa and 500 kDa dextran assays, fixed-tissue localization and diffusion control.
change_log.reason: These details explain both the evidence for reported size selectivity and the limits of its physiological interpretation.

change_log.change: Made the absence of collecting ducts and urine drainage explicit in the technical barriers and interpretation of the demonstrated result.
change_log.reason: The review identified drainage as a concrete reason the reported tissue cannot be treated as a replacement kidney.

change_log.change: Distinguished the published component demonstration from future clinical manufacturing goals and from evidence of human renal replacement.
change_log.reason: The supplied study was nonclinical and did not demonstrate durable human-scale organ function.

change_log.change: Preserved full-text access while specifying uninspected figures, movies and datasets, partial supplementary extraction and the absence of a freshness record.
change_log.reason: Access to article text supports the dated finding without establishing independent visual verification or comprehensive field coverage through 1 November 2026.

change_log.change: Strengthened the proposed completion test with independent replication, prespecified endpoints, attribution of recipient function and explicit production and cost targets.
change_log.reason: These additions make the proposal more assessable without inventing numerical thresholds or presenting it as a consensus standard.

change_log.change: Retained the two-organ proposal while clarifying its purpose and finite scope.
change_log.reason: Kidney and liver demonstrations would test generality, but would neither establish literal universality nor imply that liver manufacture has already been demonstrated.

change_log.change: Separated conditional clinical impact from findings directly documented by the kidney study and explained distinctions across the supplied roster.
change_log.reason: Supply transformation, access and relationships to other innovations are reasoned implications, not experimental outcomes of the supplied source.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record does not establish the latest field-wide state through 1 November 2026; the dated study should not be treated as an exhaustive survey.

Figures, movies and underlying datasets were not independently inspected, and supplementary extraction was partial. Those materials could provide additional experimental detail beyond the reviewed text.
The supplied evidence does not establish physiological filtration thresholds, long-term function, human-scale renal replacement or a drainage solution for the reported organoids.
No evidence for manufactured liver replacement or another whole-organ type is supplied; the two-organ completion criterion remains a proposal.
Organ-specific follow-up durations, safety and functional endpoints, acceptable comparisons with conventional transplantation, and production throughput and total-cost targets remain undefined.

brief.title: Human organs made for transplantation when needed
possible: People who need a transplant could receive a manufactured organ that keeps them alive over the long term. Production could follow a predictable schedule based on clinical need, allowing patients and care teams to plan treatment.
why: Transplantation could depend less on finding a suitable donor organ. A dependable supply could reduce some waiting delays and make treatment schedules more predictable for patients and transplant teams.

sources.showed: They increased production of kidney organoids, small lab-grown tissues with kidney structures and blood vessels. After implantation in mice, the tissue filtered test molecules according to size.
sources.quote: Here, we have developed a cost-effective mass-production method for manufacturing vascularized kidney organoids, which has improved production efficiency by more than 50 times compared to conventional culture systems.
sources.cited_for: The work connects larger-scale tissue production with an early demonstration of kidney filtering.
sources.not_established: The tissue could not drain urine and did not demonstrate lasting replacement of kidney function.

sources.who: Hisanobu Higashi, Hiroshi Yagi and colleagues
sources.showed: They populated a pig liver's supporting structure with liver cells and cells lining blood vessels. The resulting human-scale graft improved liver function when implanted alongside the existing liver in pigs with liver failure.
sources.quote: It was observed that the auxiliary bioengineered liver graft improved liver function for 28 days and exhibited upregulation of liver-specific genes.
sources.cited_for: A human-scale engineered liver graft provided functional support in a large animal.
sources.not_established: Supporting an existing liver in pigs does not establish durable replacement of a human liver.

sources.showed: They removed cells from rat, pig and human kidneys, preserving supporting structures and fluid channels. Rat kidneys rebuilt with cells produced rudimentary urine in laboratory tests and after transplantation.
sources.quote:
When transplanted in orthotopic position in rat, the grafts were perfused by the recipient’s 
circulation, and produced urine via the ureteral conduit in vivo.
sources.cited_for: Rebuilt rat kidneys received blood from recipients and drained urine through the tube connecting kidney to bladder.
sources.not_established: Preserving a human kidney's structure does not establish a functioning human replacement; the rebuilt kidneys were tested in rats.

sources.showed: They rebuilt rat lungs by adding cells to preserved lung structures. Transplanted lungs connected to recipients' blood supply and airways exchanged gases for up to 6 hours.
sources.quote:
By day 5, constructs could 
be perfused with blood and ventilated using physiologic 
pressures, and they generated gas exchange comparable to 
that of isolated native lungs.
sources.cited_for: Engineered lungs demonstrated gas exchange after transplantation in rats.
sources.not_established: Brief gas exchange in rats does not establish durable, human-scale lung replacement.

shown: Researchers have demonstrated parts of organ function in animals. Tekguc and colleagues grew kidney tissues that filtered test molecules in mice. Song and colleagues rebuilt rat kidneys that produced urine, while Ott and colleagues rebuilt rat lungs that exchanged gases briefly.

Higashi, Yagi and colleagues built a human-scale liver graft that improved liver function in pigs for 28 days. It supported the animals' existing livers. These animal studies have not demonstrated durable manufactured organs that replace failing organs in people.
missing: Complete human-scale organs still need to combine their essential functions, blood supply and necessary drainage over the long term.
The kidney organoids that filtered test molecules still lacked collecting ducts, the channels needed to drain urine.
Independent teams still need to reproduce manufacturing and lasting recipient function across different vital organ types.
A clinical process still needs consistent production, checks before transplantation, and lasting safety and function in recipients.

milestones.label: Manufactured human-scale organs reliably sustain life
milestones.explanation: Repeatedly manufactured human-scale organs would have to provide lasting, coordinated function in recipients, with their contribution measured separately. This would establish that the organs themselves sustain life.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce success in two vital organ types
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce manufacturing and recipient function for at least two vital organ types. This would establish that the capability extends beyond a single organ type.

milestones.label: Clinical outcomes and production meet predefined targets
milestones.explanation: Each organ type would need defined follow-up, safety and function comparisons with donor transplants, plus consistent production and targets for output and total manufacturing and care costs. This would establish practical clinical usefulness.

uncertain: The requirement for success in two organ types is a proposed test of breadth, rather than an agreed scientific standard.
Required follow-up, acceptable differences from donor transplants, production output and total-cost targets remain undefined.
The kidney filtering results do not yet establish how effectively the tissue could clear waste from the body.

page.title: Bioengineered solid organs for transplantation
page.definition: A kidney, liver, heart or lung manufactured from human cells can be transplanted to replace a failing organ’s functions. Bioengineering combines living cells with supporting structures, a blood supply and the connections required for the organ to function in its recipient.

goal.need: In the United States in 2024, 167,230 unique patients were on a solid-organ transplant waiting list during the year; OPTN/SRTR reports 46,750 solid-organ transplants. Manufacturing replacement organs from cells is an explicit objective of ARPA-H’s PRINT programme.

figures.caption: US organ-specific waiting-list additions and transplants in 2024
figures.note: Annual additions and transplant counts are different populations; their difference is not a count of patients left waiting.

statements.body: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health
statements.quote: Program aims to restore normal tissue function and eliminate lengthy transplant wait times
statements.context: The announcement launches PRINT, a programme for manufacturing organs using bioprinting and regenerative medicine.

statements.quote: we seek to engineer organs using porcine organ scaffolds combined with human donor (allogeneic) cells to produce human-like organs.
statements.context: The passage describes the developer’s allogeneic regenerative-medicine programme; allogeneic cells come from another person.

statements.body: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, PRINT programme
statements.quote: Demonstrate viability and longevity of the bioprinted organ in large animal model (3–6-month survival).
statements.context: Milestone M3.10 also specifies implantation in more than 5 large animals and safety assessment at 6 months. These are programme targets for bioprinted kidney, heart and liver candidates.

completion.title: FDA licenses a manufactured human-cell solid organ for transplantation as a replacement organ.
completion.criterion: FDA issues a biologics licence for a manufactured human-cell kidney, liver, heart or lung whose approved indication is organ replacement by transplantation. The licensing decision establishes the product’s safety, effectiveness and quality and the suitability of its manufacturing facilities. Each organ case is assessed separately.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, CBER’s published biologics-licensing requirements; this test uses the US cellular-biologic pathway.
completion.threshold_quote: If the agency determines that the data adequately demonstrate the product's safety, effectiveness, and quality, and that the manufacturing facility meets required standards
completion.basis: Licensure combines evidence of benefit in people with manufacturing quality and facility requirements. It therefore tests both replacement-organ performance and controlled production. FDA’s published list of licensed cellular and gene therapy products contains no manufactured kidney, liver, heart or lung.

milestones.title: A bioengineered organ prototype demonstrates its intended biological activity in a nonclinical model.
milestones.criterion: Identify the prototype’s principal intended effects in a suitable laboratory or animal model using justified measures of biological activity. Song and colleagues reported urine production after transplantation of recellularized rat kidneys on 14 April 2013. Ott and colleagues reported gas exchange by recellularized rat lungs, including measurements 6 hours after transplantation, on 13 July 2010. The main articles do not specify the transplant-group sample sizes. These results demonstrate component functions.
milestones.set_by: European Medicines Agency, Guideline on Human Cell-Based Medicinal Products, section 4.3.1; a general nonclinical proof-of-principle recommendation.
milestones.threshold_quote: The principal effects should be identified in non-clinical studies in a suitable model in vitro or in vivo.

milestones.title: A bioengineered organ’s preclinical results support reasonably safe initiation of a human transplant study.
milestones.criterion: Pharmacology and toxicology establish a basis for reasonably safe clinical investigation using the proposed product and implantation procedure. Cell–scaffold products require functional, structural, biocompatibility and safety assessment, with observation long enough to assess durability. Partial evidence: Higashi and colleagues’ 2022 auxiliary liver study reported improved function over 28 days in pigs: 7 graft recipients and 3 controls; 2 recipients died from surgical complications before day 28. This was support of a remaining native liver.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Preclinical Assessment of Investigational Cellular and Gene Therapy Products, sections II and IV.E, including the IND standard in 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8).
milestones.threshold_quote: the sponsor has concluded that it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: A bioengineered replacement organ is transplanted into a living participant under an effective IND.
milestones.criterion: Implant the manufactured organ in a living participant in a clinical investigation under an effective Investigational New Drug application, the authorization for experimental administration. FDA permits an IND to take effect after 30 calendar days without a clinical hold, or earlier notification. Related human evidence remains external support: on 26 January 2026, United Therapeutics announced treatment of 5 liver-failure patients with miroliverELAP for at least 44 hours and safety follow-up over 32 days. This non-peer-reviewed announcement concerns an organ outside the body and does not satisfy the implantation test.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(a), defining initial introduction into humans, and its published IND review procedure.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: A bioengineered organ demonstrates clinical effectiveness and manufacturing quality sufficient for licensing.
milestones.criterion: Clinical investigations establish effectiveness for the proposed organ-replacement indication: two adequate, well-controlled investigations, or one such investigation plus sufficient confirmatory evidence, as FDA describes. Manufacturing studies provide product-specific evidence of process performance, release specifications and quality control sufficient to support the licence application. FDA specifies no minimum number of process-qualification batches and can permit some qualification activities after licensing. Clinical endpoints, sample size and follow-up depend on the product and indication.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, August 2026 cellular-therapy development guidance, questions 33–34, and May 2026 manufacturing guidance, section III.B.
milestones.threshold_quote: one adequate and well-controlled clinical study plus confirmatory evidence is sufficient to establish effectiveness.

not_found: No published human transplantation study of a manufactured human-cell kidney, liver, heart or lung was identified.
No cross-organ consensus defining production on demand or requiring demonstrations in multiple organ types was found in FDA/EMA guidance, PRINT documents or the developer roadmap.
Full-text access to Tekguc and colleagues’ 2026 kidney-organoid article was blocked at Nature and PMC.
The 2026 Liver Meeting abstract reporting miroliverELAP results could not be opened.

results.finding: Human kidney organoid nephron sheets, implanted in 6 experiments, showed selective filtration of 3 kDa dextran in mice.
results.detail: Sheets were implanted in mouse dorsal skinfold chambers. Imaging and tissue analysis supported size-selective filtration; the organoids lacked collecting ducts and could not drain urine.
results.quote: Within 30–60 min post-dextran injection, we observed the pooling of LMW dextran, while HMW dextran did not show similar behavior, indicating the differential distribution of these molecules within the interstitial spaces of the nephron sheet

results.finding: Auxiliary bioengineered liver grafts improved liver function over 28 days in pigs; 7 received grafts and 3 were controls.
results.detail: Two graft recipients died from surgical complications before day 28. The graft supported a remaining native liver.
results.quote: It was observed that the auxiliary bioengineered liver graft improved liver function for 28 days and exhibited upregulation of liver-specific genes.

results.finding: In a preclinical study, 7 pigs received auxiliary grafts and 3 were controls; grafts improved liver function over 28 days.
results.detail: Two recipients died from surgical complications before day 28. The grafts supported native livers, used porcine cells, and developed portal-vein stenosis; the study does not establish safety for a human replacement-organ trial.
results.quote: It was observed that the auxiliary bioengineered liver graft improved liver function for 28 days and exhibited upregulation of liver-specific genes.

results.finding: Transplanted bioengineered rat kidneys produced urine at 1.2±0.1 μl/min; transplant sample size not reported.
results.detail: The grafts demonstrated a component of kidney function, but urine output and creatinine clearance were lower than in native controls.
results.quote:
Regenerated kidneys produced less urine than native kidneys (1.2±0.1 vs. 3.2±0.9 μl min−1 
in native controls, 4.9±1.4 μl min−1 in decellularized kidneys)

results.finding: Transplanted bioengineered rat kidneys showed no signs of clot formation or bleeding; sample size not reported.
results.detail: These acute observations provide preliminary safety evidence, but do not establish durability or a sufficient safety basis for a human transplant study.
results.quote:
Orthotopic transplantation of regenerated kidneys showed immediate graft function during 
blood perfusion via the recipient’s vasculature in vivo without signs of clot formation or 
bleeding.

results.finding: Transplanted bioengineered rat lungs, sample size not stated, showed gas exchange at 6 hours.
results.detail: Arterial oxygen tension was higher in recipients than in pneumonectomized controls. The grafts demonstrated a component function, with edema developing over several hours.
results.quote:
Blood gas analyses
obtained 6 h after transplantation, with the rats breathing room air,
revealed significantly higher arterial blood oxygen tension in recipi-
ents of regenerated lungs compared to that in pneumonectomized
controls (127 ± 18 mm Hg versus 72 ± 12 mm Hg, P = 0.011)

results.finding: Transplanted bioengineered rat lungs, sample size not stated, were observed for 6 hours.
results.detail: The study reported short-term function and graft findings, including edema, but did not establish the pharmacology, toxicology or durability needed to support a human transplant study.
results.quote:
A group of rats was allowed to recover after the acute experiment,
successfully extubated after transplantation and maintained without
ventilatory support for 6 h after transplantation.

results.finding: A bioengineered kidney implanted in a pig (n=1) produced urine with approximately 1% hematocrit.
results.detail: The graft showed filtration for up to 5 hours. The study focused on glomerular filtration; it did not incorporate renal tubular cells or assess tubular function.
results.quote:
While implant 3 only tested a single-
BEK, this implant extended the examination window up to 5 hours,
demonstrating sustained ﬁltration function with remarkably low (around
1%) urine hematocrit and lower urine protein levels compared to serum
protein levels (Fig. 7a, b).

results.finding: Human iPSC-derived mini livers remained functional for 4 days after transplantation in rats; sample size not stated.
results.detail: The text does not identify the liver functions observed or the measures used to assess biological activity.
results.quote: The regenerated human iPSC-derived mini liver containing multiple cell types was tested in vivo and remained functional for 4 days after auxiliary liver transplantation in immunocompromised, engineered (IL2rg−/−) rats.

results.finding: Partially recellularized human heart scaffold (number of hearts unspecified; 6 pressure pulses): developed pressure of 2.4 ± 0.1 mmHg.
results.detail: After 14 days in bioreactor culture, electrically stimulated myocardium generated left ventricular pressure. Only part of the scaffold was recellularized; the result demonstrates a component function.
results.quote: stimulated myocardial contractions generated developed pressures of 2.4 ± 0.1 mmHg

results.finding: Human-cell bioartificial lungs transplanted into pigs (n=3) showed a pulmonary artery-to-vein PO₂ gradient of 178 ± 153 mm Hg.
results.detail: Gas exchange was evident immediately after transplantation. At 24 hours after reperfusion, pulmonary arteries were occluded with thrombus in all bioartificial lungs.
results.quote: The gas exchange function was evident immediately after transplantation; PO 2  gradient between pulmonary artery and vein were 178 ± 153 mm Hg in the bioartificial lung group and 183 ± 117 mm Hg in the control group.

results.finding: Transplanted bioartificial rat lungs (sample size not stated) provided oxygenation for up to 7 days.
results.detail: Oxygenation was comparable to cadaveric lung transplants. Gas exchange subsequently declined with progressive graft consolidation and inflammation.
results.quote: After using improved graft preservation and postoperative weaning protocols, animals could be fully recovered, and bioartificial lung constructs provided oxygenation as long as 7 days at levels comparable to cadaveric lung transplants.
